_doc: Feature 0091 §6.1 — the lineage evidence wire contract, as DATA.
READ BY BOTH SIDES, ON PURPOSE. The Go backend writes `request` and reads
`result`; the Python agent reads `request` and writes `result`. Neither
side owns both halves, so neither side's own tests can catch a rename:
before this file, Python could have renamed `lineage_checks` to anything
and Go's parser would have gone on returning an empty slice with no error
and no log line, silently disabling every LLM-tier closure in the fleet.
The pin is that ONE file is asserted against by TWO suites:
A key renamed on either side fails that side's assertion against this
file. Editing this file to make a test pass just moves the failure to the
other language — which is the point.
Every value below was GENERATED by the shipped code, not hand-written:
